**Check:** The $k$-th term is $\sin\frac{(2k-1)\pi}{24}\sin\frac{(2k+3)\pi}{24}$ for $k=1,\dots,10$. The product-to-sum identity gives

$$\sin A\sin B=\tfrac12\left[\cos\tfrac{\pi}{6}-\cos\tfrac{(2k+1)\pi}{12}\right],$$

so the sum is $\tfrac12\left[5\sqrt{3}-\sum_{k=1}^{10}\cos\tfrac{(2k+1)\pi}{12}\right]$.

The angles $\tfrac{(2k+1)\pi}{12}$ for $k=1,\dots,10$ are $3,5,\dots,21$ (times $\pi/12$). Their cosines pair off to zero except for the two terms at $5\pi/12$ and $7\pi/12$... more precisely, the 5th and 6th angles contribute $-\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}$ each, so the cosine sum is $-\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2}$. Hence

$$\frac12\left[5\sqrt3+\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2}\right]=\frac{5\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}.$$

Direct numerical evaluation of the ten terms (≈ 0.0795, 0.3036, 0.5625, 0.7866, 0.9159, each repeated symmetrically) gives ≈ 5.296, which confirms this.
